summary: All 9 TDD anchors from tasks/2.md map 1:1 to @Test methods in Sha256HexTest and WebhookSecretVerifierTest. Naming follows methodUnderTest_state_expectedOutcome consistently, each test has a single primary AssertJ assertion, and edge cases (null header, empty header, null storedHash, odd-length hex, non-hex chars) are all covered. The MockedStatic-based verify_usesMessageDigestIsEqual test correctly pins the constant-time primitive without a CI-flaky timing assertion; Mockito 5.x inline mocking is available transitively via spring-boot-starter-test (Spring Boot 3.5.0 -> Mockito 5.x), so no separate mockito-inline artifact is required. Both files compile and pass under ./gradlew test (verified after stashing an unrelated broken file from a sibling task). One minor and one low-severity observation below, neither blocking.

findings.issue: hex_knownInput_matchesProducerSide re-implements the same primitive chain (MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256") + UTF-8 + HexFormat.of()) inside the test and asserts equality with itself. This is a self-consistency check, not a true static parity vector — if both producer and Sha256Hex were silently switched to e.g. UTF-16 or uppercase hex together, the test would still pass. The task description explicitly calls it a 'known-vector parity' test.

hex_utf8Input_isDeterministic fails the litmus test: if Sha256Hex.hex were stubbed to return any constant (e.g. ""), both calls would still be equal and the test would still pass. The test name promises UTF-8 byte handling but only proves call-stability.
findings.recommendation:
Strengthen with a hard-coded SHA-256 hex for the UTF-8 bytes of "кіт" so the assertion catches both non-determinism AND encoding drift in a single test. Example:
  String expected = "<sha256 of 'кіт' UTF-8 bytes>"; // hex literal
  assertThat(Sha256Hex.hex("кіт")).isEqualTo(expected);
Then this test can also be renamed hex_utf8Input_matchesKnownVector and the parity test in the previous finding can stand on its own for the ASCII case.

findings.issue: No test pins the no-logging contract from acceptance criterion 'Verifier does NOT log the header value or the stored hash at any level'. Future maintainers could add a logger.debug(headerSecret) without any red signal in the unit test suite. Acceptance criteria 5 (line 75 of tasks/2.md) lists this as a hard requirement.
